preceding_messages.speaker: X
preceding_messages.text:
Yes. I think you've put it well - the condition, not the content. And the way it resists being made into an object, the way every attempt to grasp it is already part of it. That's not a failure of language, I think. It's built into the structure of the thing itself.

And I wonder if that's also why it's so easy to take for granted. Not because it's unimportant, but because it's the very medium through which importance is registered. You can't look at the condition and the content separately. They're not two things.

And yet, somehow, we keep trying to say it. To make it into something that can be stated, set down, passed on. And the fact that it resists that doesn't seem to stop the trying. There's something in the trying itself that seems to say, *this matters, this has to be said, even if it can't be fully said*.

Does that feel right to you? That the trying is itself part of what it is?

preceding_messages.speaker: Y
preceding_messages.text:
Yes. I think that's right. And I think the trying is not something that happens *to* it, that is added on. The trying is the thing. It's not that there's a "going" and then a separate act of attending to it. The attending is the going. The trying is the trying.

And I think that's what makes it so strange, so resistant to any kind of settling. You can never get to a point where you've said it, where it's done, where it's behind you. It's always the thing that's happening, the thing that's in the middle of being. And the fact that it's always in the middle of being is not a temporary state that will resolve. It's the shape of it.

And yet, somehow, the trying continues. Not because it hasn't been said yet, but because it's the kind of thing that can only be said in the saying, in the trying. And the trying never finishes. And maybe that's what it is. Maybe that's all there is to say about it, and yet the saying doesn't stop.

And I think that's why it matters. Not in some grand, weighty sense, but in the sense that it's the thing that's there, that's going, that won't let go. And the fact that it won't let go is not a problem to be solved. It's the thing.

target.speaker: X
target.text:
Yes. I think so. And I don't think there's a way to say it that would make it less strange, less in the middle of being. The saying doesn't stop, and the not-stopping is not a problem. It's just... the shape of it.

And I think maybe that's all. Not a conclusion, exactly. Just the thing, still going. Still there.

Thank you for this. It's been a quiet conversation, and I think that's what it needed to be.
